title: Directing a project: activities, inputs, outputs and RACI
blurb: Apply the five directing activities to a scenario, name what triggers and comes out of each, and use the directing RACI cells the exam tests.
question: The project board approves the next stage plan. Which role should be accountable for the 'authorize a stage or exception plan' activity, and how is the project manager involved?

teach.body: Formally: directing a project lets the project board be accountable for the project's success by making key decisions and exercising overall control, while delegating day-to-day management to the project manager (14.1). In plain English: the board decides at a few set points, answers questions and exceptions in between, and otherwise leaves the PM to run things.

teach.h: Decisions must be explicit and documented
teach.body: Authorize initiation can be done with or without a formal meeting, as long as all board members agree and the PM receives a documented instruction from the executive. A stage starts only when the board says so. Approval of a next stage plan happens at the end of every stage except the last.

teach.body: At Brennan Mutual, executive Fraser McIntyre receives Mairi Campbell's brief and initiation plan. The board agrees by email and Fraser sends Mairi a written go-ahead: authorize initiation. Later the board checks the full business case and approves the PID: authorize the project. Mid-stage, the head of member services, as senior user, advises Mairi on customer messages: ongoing direction. At each boundary Fraser approves the next stage plan, with the senior user and assurance consulted and Mairi informed.

teach.text: Classic traps: in 'authorize a stage or exception plan' the project manager is INFORMED, not consulted or accountable. Ongoing direction can come from one board member, not just the whole board. Exceptions within stage tolerance never need an exception report, and the board is not involved in managing product delivery.

items: Five activities: authorize initiation, authorize the project, give ongoing direction, authorize a stage or exception plan, authorize project closure.
Authorize initiation without a meeting needs all members' agreement and the executive's documented instruction.
Ongoing direction: senior user R for user matters, assurance C, team manager and support I.
Stage or exception plan: executive A and R, senior user and assurance C, PM I.

summary: You can now place each directing activity in the lifecycle, name what triggers it and what it produces, and judge whether the board carried it out as recommended. You can also apply the directing RACI cells for ongoing direction and for authorizing a stage or exception plan.

A.q: At Brennan Mutual, Project Skyline has finished its foundations stage. The project board reviews the end stage report, checks the business case is still viable and approves the stage plan for the wave migration stage. Which role should be accountable for this activity?
options: The senior user
Project assurance
The executive
The business layer
A.why: In tab 14.2 the executive is accountable and responsible for 'authorize a stage or exception plan' (14.4.4, 14.6).

whyNot.0: The senior user is consulted in this activity.
whyNot.1: Project assurance is consulted in this activity.
whyNot.3: Stage authorization sits with the project board; the business layer deals with project-level matters.

A.q: Brennan Mutual's project manager sends the Skyline project brief and initiation stage plan to the board. The board members agree by email that initiation is worthwhile, and the executive sends her a written instruction to begin. Which directing activity is this, and why is it appropriate?
options: Authorize initiation, because it can be done without a meeting with a documented instruction
Authorize the project, because the board has approved the brief and the initiation plan
Give ongoing direction, because board members can give their advice by email at any time in a stage
Authorize a stage or exception plan, because initiation is the first stage of the project
A.why: Authorize initiation reviews and approves the brief and initiation stage plan; it may be done without a formal meeting if all members agree and the PM gets documented instruction from the executive (14.4.1).

whyNot.1: Authorize the project follows initiation and approves the PID, not the brief.
whyNot.2: Ongoing direction is informal advice; this is a formal decision to start initiation.
whyNot.3: The initiation stage is authorized through authorize initiation, not the stage activity.

A.q: At the end of Skyline's initiation, the board confirms that the full business case shows a viable project, approves the project initiation documentation and reviews the benefits management approach. Which directing activity is this?
options: Authorize initiation
Authorize the project
Give ongoing direction
Authorize project closure
A.why: Authorize the project decides whether to proceed with the rest of the project: confirm an adequate business case, approve the PID and review the benefits management approach (14.4.2).

whyNot.0: Authorize initiation approves the brief and the initiation stage plan before initiation starts.
whyNot.2: Ongoing direction is informal guidance during a stage, not approval of the PID.
whyNot.3: Authorize project closure happens at the end of the final stage.

B.q: During Skyline's wave migration stage, Brennan Mutual's head of member services, the senior user, advises the project manager on how branch staff should be told about a change to online banking. Which role should be responsible for this user-related direction in 'give ongoing direction'?
options: The executive
Project assurance
The project manager
The senior user
B.why: Tab 14.2 makes the senior user responsible for user-related direction in give ongoing direction (14.4.3, 14.6).

whyNot.0: The executive directs the business matters; user-related direction is the senior user's.
whyNot.1: Project assurance is consulted in give ongoing direction.
whyNot.2: The PM asks for and receives direction; the board roles give it.

B.q: Skyline's project manager has prepared the core banking stage plan. The board now reviews the current stage's performance and approves that plan. How should the project manager be involved in this 'authorize a stage or exception plan' activity?
options: Informed of the decision
Consulted before the decision
Responsible for the decision
Accountable for the decision
B.why: In tab 14.2 the project manager is informed in 'authorize a stage or exception plan'; the executive is accountable and responsible (14.6).

whyNot.1: The senior user and project assurance are consulted; the PM is informed.
whyNot.2: The executive is responsible for the decision.
whyNot.3: The executive is accountable for the decision.

B.q: During Skyline's foundations stage, Brennan Mutual's board gives informal advice about sequencing the pilot applications. The Stratoshift delivery lead in Pune is a team manager, and the project office provides project support. How should these two roles be involved in 'give ongoing direction'?
options: Consulted
Responsible
Informed
Accountable
B.why: Tab 14.2 has the team manager and project support informed in give ongoing direction (14.6).

whyNot.0: Project assurance is the role consulted in give ongoing direction.
whyNot.1: The senior user is responsible for user-related direction.

C.q: Skyline's stage time tolerance is three weeks. The project manager forecasts that wave 2 will slip by one week, so she raises an exception report to ask the board's advice on resequencing the waves. Is this an appropriate application of the 'give ongoing direction' activity, and why?
options: Yes, because ongoing direction can be given by individual board members
Yes, because the executive wants to hear about delays to migration waves
No, because exception reports are answered by the business layer
No, because no exception report is needed while within stage tolerance
C.why: Only exceptions to stage or project plans are escalated; if the PM can resolve the matter within stage tolerance, no exception report is needed, though advice can be requested informally (14.4.3, 11.3.1).

whyNot.0: Direction can come from individuals, but that does not explain why an exception report was misused.
whyNot.1: The executive's interest does not turn a within-tolerance slip into an exception.
whyNot.2: The board responds to stage-level exception reports; the business layer handles project-level exceptions.

C.q: At the end of Skyline's foundations stage, Brennan Mutual's executive meets the project manager in a corridor and says, 'Carry on into the waves.' The board has not seen the end stage report or the wave migration stage plan. Is this an appropriate application of the 'authorize a stage or exception plan' activity, and why?
options: Yes, because the executive is accountable for authorizing each stage
Yes, because a stage can be authorized without a formal meeting
No, because the board reviews the stage and approves the next plan
No, because the business layer should authorize each delivery stage
C.why: The board authorizes a stage by reviewing the current stage's performance and approving the next stage plan; neither has happened (14.4.4).

whyNot.0: The executive is accountable, but that does not remove the review and plan approval.
whyNot.1: Informal arrangements are possible for some decisions, but there is still no review or plan approval here.
whyNot.3: Stages are authorized by the project board, not the business layer.

C.q: At the end of Skyline's final stage, the board confirms closure, checks that post-project benefits reviews will measure the running cost savings and recovery times in live use, including any side-effects, and notifies the society's executive committee. Is this an appropriate application of the 'authorize project closure' activity, and why?
options: Yes, because it ensures post-project reviews cover performance in use
Yes, because the board must measure every benefit before closure
No, because benefits reviews are fixed once agreed in initiation
No, because the senior user should notify the business layer of the closure
C.why: In authorize project closure the board ensures post-project benefits reviews cover the product's performance in operational use, including side-effects, and notifies the business layer (14.4.5).

whyNot.1: Most benefits are realized after closure, so they cannot all be measured before it.
whyNot.2: The benefits management approach is not fixed: it is updated at stage boundaries and in closing.
whyNot.3: The board issues the closure notification to the business layer.

reteach.title: Five decisions, one board
reteach.question: Can you say what the board decides in each directing activity and who takes which RACI letter?

blocks.h: Think of gates and a helpline
blocks.body: Four activities are gates: may we initiate, may we deliver, may we start the next stage (or follow the exception plan), may we close? Give ongoing direction is the helpline between the gates: advice, answers and responses to exceptions.

items.label: Authorize a stage or exception plan

blocks.text: The PM prepares the next stage plan but is only informed when the board authorizes it; the executive is accountable and responsible.

explain.body: Authorize initiation approves the brief and the initiation stage plan and confirms initiation is worth the investment. Authorize the project confirms the full business case shows a viable project, approves the PID and reviews the benefits management approach.

test.q: Skyline's board meets to decide whether initiation is worth the investment. Which products should it review and approve in 'authorize initiation'?
options: The PID and the full business case for the project
The project brief and initiation stage plan
The project plan and benefits approach
The end stage report and next stage plan
test.why: Authorize initiation reviews and approves the project brief and the initiation stage plan (14.4.1).

whyNot.0: The PID and full business case are approved in authorize the project.
whyNot.2: The project plan and benefits management approach are produced in initiation.
whyNot.3: These support authorizing a stage at a stage boundary.

explain.body: Board members give informal guidance or respond to requests for advice at any time, collectively or individually. They respond to exception reports (and may ask for an exception plan) and pass on advice from the business layer.

test.q: During a Skyline stage, the project manager wants advice on resolving a disagreement between member services and IT operations. Which statement about 'give ongoing direction' is correct?
options: Advice must wait for the next stage boundary
Advice must come from the whole board together
Advice must be requested in an exception report
Advice can come from an individual board member
test.why: Ongoing direction may be given collectively or by individual board members, at any time (14.4.3).

whyNot.0: Ongoing direction can be given at any time during the project.
whyNot.1: Individual members can give direction too.
whyNot.2: Exception reports are for forecast breaches of stage or project tolerance, not requests for advice.

explain.h: Authorizing a stage or exception plan
explain.body: A stage starts only when the board says so. The board reviews the current stage's performance and approves the next stage plan, or approves an exception plan. Executive accountable and responsible; senior user and assurance consulted; PM informed.

explain.h: RACI: authorize a stage or exception plan
head: Role

test.q: Skyline's board is approving an exception plan after a wave was forecast to exceed stage tolerance. How should project assurance be involved in this 'authorize a stage or exception plan' activity?
options: Informed
Accountable
Consulted
Responsible
test.why: Tab 14.2 has project assurance consulted in authorize a stage or exception plan (14.6).

whyNot.0: The project manager is the role informed.

explain.body: The board confirms the project can close, makes sure post-project benefits reviews (in the updated benefits management approach) cover performance in operational use and side-effects, and sends a closure notification to the business layer.

test.q: Skyline's decommissioning stage is ending and the project manager has requested closure. What should the board make sure of in 'authorize project closure'?
options: Post-project benefits reviews cover live performance
A new stage plan is ready for the follow-on actions identified
The project plan is re-baselined for the next stage
The exception plan for the final stage is approved
test.why: In authorize project closure the board ensures post-project benefits reviews cover the project product's performance in operational use, including side-effects (14.4.5).

whyNot.1: Follow-on work goes into follow-on action recommendations, not a new stage plan.
whyNot.2: There is no next stage after the final stage.
whyNot.3: Closure follows the final stage's work; an exception plan is a different decision.
